findings.title: Obstacle and remedy share an open cadence
findings.claim: The indefinite accusative form of barrenness and the indefinite accusative form of the requested guardian make the stated obstacle and requested remedy echo one another.
findings.mechanism: The predicate `عَاقِرًا` and final `وَلِيًّا` carry the same indefinite accusative cadence; that matching form links the condition needing remedy to the concrete thing asked for.
findings.reader_payoff: The request sounds grammatically attached to the obstacle rather than appended as an unrelated wish.
findings.containment: The cadence links the two phrases; it does not make grammar predict fulfillment or replace the biological sense.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct word-analysis and cadence evidence for both forms.

findings.title: Invariable predicate form
findings.claim: The masculine-looking `عاقرا` grammatically predicates the wife's state without changing the subject or referring to another person.
findings.mechanism: The supplied morphology treats the active-participle adjective as invariable here; feminine subject agreement is carried by `كانت`, while the predicate remains accusative.
findings.reader_payoff: The surface form can be heard as a grammatical state assignment instead of a mismatch.
findings.containment: This explains the form of the predicate and does not introduce a second referent.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies explicit morphology and word-analysis evidence.

findings.title: Barrenness as the predicate
findings.claim: `عاقرا` is the accusative predicate that names the wife's established barren state.
findings.mechanism: Placed after the feminine perfect copula, the active participle functions as the state assigned to the wife, so the clause names a condition rather than an action she performs.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel where the sentence places the obstacle: in the wife's state.
findings.containment: The predicate specifies infertility in this wife context and does not generalize the form beyond the supplied clause.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct case, copular, and active-participle analysis.

findings.title: The marked obstacle returns
findings.claim: The uncommon barren-state descriptor is marked as a recurring obstacle within the supplied scene rather than a passing adjective.
findings.mechanism: The active-participle word is singled out by its rarity and supplied later recurrence; that return keeps the same obstacle visible as the story develops.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the word as a deliberate hinge in the birth request and its later confirmation.
findings.containment: The recurrence marks the obstacle's narrative weight; it does not by itself specify how the later event is fulfilled.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies the rarity and recurrence evidence directly.

findings.title: Cut-off pressure in barrenness
findings.claim: The infertility sense carries a bounded pressure of generative continuity being cut off.
findings.mechanism: The wife and birth setting activates biological infertility in `عاقرا`; the supplied cutting and hamstringing range then colors that state as interrupted generative continuity while the local sense remains barrenness.
findings.reader_payoff: Barrenness becomes perceptible as a break in a line that the petition asks to have continued.
findings.containment: The biological reading stays primary; the cutting pressure is a qualified coloring, not a claim of physical injury in the scene.

epistemic.reason: The packet explicitly marks the broader cutting pressure as narrowed under the local infertility sense.

findings.title: The consequence hinge
findings.claim: The prefixed `fa` makes the imperative the consequence of the two preceding disclosures.
findings.mechanism: The result connective joins the fear clause and barren-wife clause to `hab`, so the accumulated crisis turns directly into the request.
findings.reader_payoff: The petition is heard as arising from the stated need rather than appearing as a new topic.
findings.containment: The connective supplies causal-consecutive force and does not add a separate event beyond the request.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct connective and clause-order evidence.

findings.title: Disclosure becomes supplication
findings.claim: The sentence shifts from stating the speaker's need to performing a supplication while remaining inside the same self-testimony.
findings.mechanism: The result particle is fused to the second-person imperative after the emphatic first-person disclosure; that contact turns reported pressure into an addressed request.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the grammar itself cross from explanation into prayer.
findings.containment: The speech-act shift deepens the disclosed need and does not replace it with an unrelated command.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies the result-particle and speech-act analysis.

findings.title: The compact prayer imperative
findings.claim: The compact `hab` is a marked imperative that gives the request a compressed command shape.
findings.mechanism: The weak-root imperative omits the initial weak consonant in its surface form and appears after the result particle, so a short command carries the prayer forward.
findings.reader_payoff: The request has an audible, concentrated turn rather than a diffuse wish.
findings.containment: The form is treated as an imperative in this prayer setting; no other root sense is inferred from its compactness.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies morphology and prayer-setting evidence for the form.

findings.title: A Zakariyya gift-prayer register
findings.claim: The `hab` imperative places this request inside a supplied Zakariyya prayer register in which a gift is sought from the divine giver.
findings.mechanism: The local imperative's giver-request frame meets the supplied formula and gift echoes, so the word functions as a prayer request rather than a bare lexical mention of giving.
findings.reader_payoff: The short command is heard as a recognizable form of petition.
findings.containment: The supplied parallels illuminate the register; they do not import their surrounding stories or alter this request's local content.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies formula and same-surah gift-echo evidence.

findings.title: Bestowal without exchange
findings.claim: The requested guardian is framed as an unearned divine bestowal rather than compensation or ordinary provision.
findings.mechanism: The gift sense of `hab` meets the prayer imperative and the later divine-source phrase; the contact presents the requested person as a grant without a stated exchange.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the petition asks for a gift instead of describing a solution the household can produce.
findings.containment: The finding describes the request's framing and does not claim that the gift has already been granted in this ayah.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies lexical and prayer-register evidence for free bestowal.

findings.title: A complete transfer frame
findings.claim: The phrase builds a complete gift-transfer structure: an implied giver, a beneficiary, a source, and a requested guardian as gift.
findings.mechanism: `hab` supplies the transfer, `li` marks the beneficiary, `min ladunka` supplies the source, and the final accusative noun supplies the direct object; the four relations turn a vague plea into a specified request.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see who the gift is for, where it comes from, and what is being requested.
findings.containment: The frame describes the grammar of the petition and does not add a separate transaction or human exchange.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct argument-structure and lexical-frame evidence.

findings.title: The imperative performs the request
findings.claim: The second-person command makes the utterance itself a supplication rather than a description of a future request.
findings.mechanism: `hab` is a second-person imperative addressed to God and follows the result hinge; its grammatical act is the asking.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah begin doing what it asks for.
findings.containment: The imperative is a request for a gift and does not assert that the requested result has already occurred.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies the imperative's addressee and speech-act evidence.

findings.title: Need before source
findings.claim: The first-person beneficiary phrase names Zakariyya's need before the source of the gift is named.
findings.mechanism: `li` marks the person for whom the guardian is requested and precedes `min ladunka`, so personal need enters the transfer frame before divine origin.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the prayer's personal stake before hearing where the answer will come from.
findings.containment: The order foregrounds the beneficiary and does not make Zakariyya the giver or the requested gift.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct beneficiary attachment and ordering evidence.

findings.title: Recipient distinct from gift
findings.claim: The syntax distinguishes Zakariyya as beneficiary from the requested guardian as the gift.
findings.mechanism: `li` attaches as beneficiary while `waliyyan` follows the gift imperative as its direct object; the two roles remain grammatically separate.
findings.reader_payoff: The transfer structure becomes concrete: the prayer asks something for someone.
findings.containment: The distinction clarifies roles and does not decide the identity of the requested guardian.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies direct beneficiary and direct-object attachment evidence.

findings.title: Two source attachments remain live
findings.claim: `min ladunka` can be heard as the source of the granting act or as a source-colored description of the requested guardian, while both routes keep divine nearness central.
findings.mechanism: The source preposition governs the proximity noun and the supplied attachment evidence licenses the verb-complement route alongside a cautious noun-modifying route; the two contacts converge on immediate divine origin.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold both the gift-from-nearness and guardian-from-nearness pressures without losing the petition's direction.

findings.title: Divine nearness as remedy source
findings.claim: The second source phrase makes divine nearness the origin of the requested remedy.
findings.mechanism: The preposition `min` introduces `ladunka` as a source complement of the gift verb, redirecting the petition from its stated crisis to the origin of its answer.
findings.reader_payoff: Divine nearness becomes a grammatical source relation, not only devotional atmosphere.
findings.containment: The phrase identifies the requested gift's source and does not claim that nearness is a physical location.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies source-complement and divine-nearness evidence.

findings.title: From feared aftermath to source

findings.reader_payoff: The ayah's spatial-temporal language turns toward its answer at the moment of petition.
findings.containment: The movement is a local grammatical relation and does not erase either source phrase's ordinary meaning.

findings.title: A marked immediate source

findings.mechanism: The genitive proximity noun carries the second-person suffix and follows the source preposition; that form makes the source immediate and personalized.
findings.reader_payoff: The requested answer is heard as coming from a marked nearness beyond the failed human and biological means already named.
findings.containment: The proximity force qualifies the source relation and does not invent a separate location or mechanism of giving.

findings.mechanism: The local Form I perfect and first-person suffix place the fear in the speaker, while the explicit object identifies what he fears.

findings.containment: The variant remains a contrastive counter-reading; it does not replace the aligned surface or become a second local assertion.

findings.containment: The finding concerns audible case marking and does not introduce a new semantic or agency reading.

findings.title: Affiliation can protect or threaten
